article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Morning Brief
article.dek: No new designations overnight, the board still has not flipped to Week 9, and three lines moved back — your Saturday check before Sunday's games.

items.headline: Lead: the quarterback picture stands — Sanders, Lock and Wentz start; Baltimore trades for Brissett
paragraphs: Nothing changed overnight. Friday's final designations stand, and Saturday morning's reports confirm the same three starting quarterbacks: Shedeur Sanders starts for Cleveland with Deshaun Watson still in the concussion protocol, Drew Lock starts for Seattle with Sam Darnold out, and Carson Wentz starts for Minnesota on Monday night with Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury.

The one genuinely new item is in Baltimore. The Ravens finalized a trade for Jacoby Brissett from Arizona. Lamar Jackson had surgery on his right thumb, and Tyler Huntley is out for the season with turf toe. Baltimore hosts Jacksonville on Sunday as a big underdog, and it is not yet clear who starts at quarterback — watch the inactive list.
Lock, for his part, was cleared from Seattle's final injury report on Friday after managing a right elbow injury all week. Darnold is out with quad and rib injuries and is week-to-week.
items.takeaway: Sanders starts for Cleveland, Lock starts for Seattle, Wentz starts for Minnesota on Monday night — and Baltimore just traded for Brissett with Jackson out.

items.headline: The designation rundown: Evans out, Nelson week-to-week, Kirk hurt
paragraphs: Tampa Bay's Mike Evans is ruled out for Sunday's game at Chicago. Seattle guard Quenton Nelson needs a minor knee procedure and is week-to-week — he avoids injured reserve for now, but Seattle is already down left tackle Charles Cross, so Drew Lock starts behind a patched-up line. San Francisco's Christian Kirk is dealing with a meniscus injury as the 49ers' receiver problems mount.

Those names join Friday's outs: Garrett Wilson, A.J. Brown, Brian Robinson Jr. and David Montgomery. Hunter Henry and Kyle Monangai are questionable. None of that changed overnight — these are Friday's final designations, confirmed in Saturday morning's roundup.

Official inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday, around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games. That is the next real news event — nothing else moves the board before then.
items.takeaway: Evans is out, Nelson is week-to-week after a knee procedure, Kirk has a meniscus injury — and the next real news is Sunday's inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Weather: still calm — no wind flags anywhere on Sunday
paragraphs: Saturday morning's National Weather Service pull flags zero games for wind. All nine outdoor games sit under 15 mph sustained wind. The windiest sustained wind is 13 mph in Washington, and gusts top out at 20 mph in Chicago.
Seattle gets gusts to 16 mph with a 35% chance of rain showers. New England gets gusts to 17 mph. That is calmer than Friday's read suggested — nothing here is close to a weather problem.
The Madrid game kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET under a retractable roof, Cleveland at New Orleans is indoors, and Monday night's Bills-Vikings game is indoors too. Weather is a non-factor this week.
items.takeaway: Sunday is calm: no game is flagged for wind, gusts top out at 20 mph in Chicago, and the Madrid game plays under a roof.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — no Week 9 cards, so Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: Checked the app this morning: it still shows Week 8, last observed on Monday. There are no Week 9 cards and no Week 9 market board. That means no Hit Rate, Balanced or Value card for Sunday's games yet.

So Sunday still goes through Check. Type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation of your number, not a blind override.
The board refreshes every morning and evening. When it flips to Week 9, the cards will be there. Until then, Check is how you use the app on Sunday's games.
items.takeaway: Board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards, so Sunday's prices go through Check until the board flips.

items.headline: Learn the Game: the key number
paragraphs: A key number is a margin of victory that comes up again and again. In the NFL the big ones are 3 and 7 — games land on those scores far more often than on 4, 5 or 6.

Hypothetical: say a favorite is listed at -2.5 on Friday and -3.5 on Sunday. That one-point move crossed 3, the most common winning margin in football. It matters more than a move from -4.5 to -5.5, even though that is also a full point — because the -3.5 price now needs the favorite to win by 4, while -2.5 only needed a win by 3.
The habit to build: whenever a spread moves, ask which side of 3 or 7 your price sits on. A line crossing a key number is worth more than a line moving a full point anywhere else.
items.takeaway: A line crossing 3 is worth more than a line moving a full point anywhere else — always check which side of 3 your price sits on.

items.headline: Overnight: three lines moved back
paragraphs: DraftKings numbers via Vegas Insider, updated Friday night: the Giants moved from -3.5 back to -3, back across the key number of 3. The Chiefs total climbed another point, from 47.5 to 48.5. Dallas moved from -5.5 back to -4.5.
All three moved back toward where they opened. None of it came with new team news — Friday's designations were already in. That is just the market settling on a Saturday morning.

Remember the app has not caught these moves — it still shows Week 8, so there is no Week 9 market board to compare against. If your book's number differs from these, type it into Check and let the app run your price through the model.
items.takeaway: The Giants moved back to -3, the Chiefs total climbed to 48.5, and Dallas moved back to -4.5 — all three drifted back overnight with no new team news.

items.headline: The designations are in — bet the good number now
paragraphs: Friday's designations are final, and nothing moved overnight. If your book has a good number on a Sunday game right now and Check says bet, bet now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number on Sunday — waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too, and the Sunday late rush on big-name teams usually pushes prices against you.
The only thing left to wait for is inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday. If a player you are counting on is questionable, that is the moment it resolves — check the app again then.
items.takeaway: The designations are in, so run your book's Sunday price through Check — if it says bet, bet the good number now.

items.headline: Log the losers too
paragraphs: Settlement is manual — there is no auto-settle. The tracker only works if you are honest with yourself, so log the losers too, not just the wins. A tracker that only remembers the good days is a story, not a record.
items.takeaway: The tracker only works if you're honest with yourself — log the losers too.
